milestones.label: The constitutional voting age is eighteen
milestones.population: citizens of the United States, in the amendment's own terms
whatChanges: Citizens may register and cast a ballot in federal, state and local elections from this age onward.
This is a right that opens and stays open, not a task with a closing date.
milestones.notes: The amendment names the age at which the right attaches and no age at which it ends, so this record marks an opening rather than a span with a measured close.

milestones.label: Reported voting in the youngest adult age group
milestones.population: people grouped by age in a compilation of Census Bureau survey figures, which states that those figures are a share of the total population rather than of registered voters
whatChanges: This age group reports the lowest rate of voting of any age group the compilation publishes for the most recent presidential election.
The figure is a share of everyone counted at these ages, not a share of the people who registered.
This is a snapshot of one election, and the groups between this one and the oldest are not described here.
milestones.notes: The window is the age group the compilation names and nothing wider. Until the fix pass this claim and the one about the oldest group shared a single window running between them, so a figure about the oldest group rendered beside every year from the voting age upward.

milestones.label: Reported voting in the oldest published age group
milestones.population: people grouped by age in a compilation of Census Bureau survey figures, which states that those figures are a share of the total population rather than of registered voters
whatChanges: This age group reports the highest rate of voting of any age group the compilation publishes for the most recent presidential election.
The figure is a share of everyone counted at these ages, not a share of the people who registered.
This is a snapshot of one election, and the groups between this one and the youngest are not described here.
milestones.notes: The oldest published group is open-ended at the top, so the window closes at this timeline's own ceiling rather than at a measured end.

milestones.label: Formal volunteering through an organization in the youngest band counted
milestones.population: people counted in the Current Population Survey Civic Engagement and Volunteering Supplement, whose universe runs from the teenage years upward with no top age
whatChanges: The highest reported rate of volunteering through an organization of any band the supplement counts sits in this one.
The bands between this one and the next-highest band report lower rates than either of them.
Rates here were measured during a pandemic year, which the publisher flags as a period of decline across groups.
milestones.notes: The window is the age band the publisher names and nothing wider. Until the fix pass this record ran from this band to the second-highest band, drawing the gap between two peaks as though something ran through it.

milestones.label: Formal volunteering through an organization in the mid-forties to mid-fifties
milestones.population: people counted in the Current Population Survey Civic Engagement and Volunteering Supplement, whose universe runs from the teenage years upward with no top age
whatChanges: This band reports the second highest rate of volunteering through an organization of any band the supplement counts.
The bands between this one and the teenage band report lower rates than either of them.
Rates here were measured during a pandemic year, which the publisher flags as a period of decline across groups.
milestones.notes: The window is the age band the publisher names and nothing wider. The supplement's universe has no top age, so this is not a ceiling on volunteering.

milestones.label: Daily time in leisure and sports in the mid-thirties to mid-forties
milestones.population: the population interviewed for the American Time Use Survey, averaged across all days of the year, in the single age band the release names
whatChanges: Average daily hours in leisure and sports are lower in this band than in any other band the release reports.
Leisure and sports is the survey's own category, so what falls inside it is the survey's definition rather than an everyday one.
These are averages across a population and across every day of the week, not a description of any one week.
milestones.notes: The window is the age band the release names and nothing wider. Until the fix pass this record ran from the lowest band to the highest one it was being compared with, which drew a contrast between two ends of a life as though it were a window something happens in.

milestones.label: Daily time in leisure and sports in the oldest band the survey reports
milestones.population: the population interviewed for the American Time Use Survey, averaged across all days of the year, in the oldest age band the release names
whatChanges: Average daily hours in leisure and sports are higher in this band than in any other band the release reports.
Leisure and sports is the survey's own category, so what falls inside it is the survey's definition rather than an everyday one.
These are averages across a population and across every day of the week, not a description of any one week.
milestones.notes: The release's oldest band is open-ended at the top, so the window closes at this timeline's own ceiling rather than at a measured end.

milestones.label: Reported attendance at religious services
whatChanges: Attending religious services at least monthly is reported at a higher rate in the oldest adult band of a national survey than in the youngest.
That is a comparison between bands at one moment; the bands in between are not described here.
No source fetched in this pass supports reading it as a change that happens across one life.
milestones.researchNote: Needed: a source that follows the same birth cohorts across survey dates and gives a verbatim sentence naming the ages at which religious practice changes within a cohort. The Religious Landscape Study compares two age bands at a single moment, and the same report's cohort analysis states that cohorts have not become more religious as they aged, so it cannot support a life-course window in either direction. Candidates to fetch: General Social Survey cohort trend tables on gss.norc.org; Pew cohort analyses on pewresearch.org that report the same cohort at two survey dates.
milestones.windowInWords: Attending religious services at least monthly is reported at a higher rate in the oldest adult band of a national survey than in the youngest, but that is a comparison between bands at one moment, the bands in between are not described, and no source fetched in this pass supports reading it as a change that happens across a life.

milestones.label: Having a will and an advance directive on file
milestones.population: United States adults asked what they have done in planning for their own needs as they age
milestones.careNote: This is a description of when people in a survey say they did paperwork, not a schedule anyone is measured against, and a lawyer or a clinician is the right place for a question about one person.
whatChanges: Writing a will, and naming someone to make medical decisions on a person's behalf when they cannot, is something most people report doing later in adulthood rather than early.
The share reporting each document is higher in the seventies band than in the band below it.
A will and an advance directive are two separate documents, and the survey counts them separately.
milestones.notes: The window is the band from which the publisher states most adults have both documents, and nothing wider; the survey's oldest band is open-ended at the top, so it closes at this timeline's own ceiling. Until the fix pass it began in the band where a minority report them, which rendered the seventies figure beside every year of the sixties.

milestones.label: Reported life satisfaction and sense of purpose shift across adulthood
milestones.researchNote: Needed: a nationally representative United States source reporting a life-satisfaction or sense-of-purpose measure by single year of age or by narrow age band, with a verbatim sentence naming the ages at which the measure is lowest and highest. Candidates to fetch: CDC BRFSS life satisfaction module tabulations on cdc.gov; the Health and Retirement Study data book on hrs.isr.umich.edu; NORC General Social Survey trend reports on gss.norc.org. Pew and Gallup summaries are acceptable only with the primary survey named.
milestones.windowInWords: Self-reported life satisfaction is often described as dipping somewhere in midlife and rising again in later life, but no source fetched in this pass gave a verbatim sentence naming the ages at which it turns, so no window is asserted.

milestones.label: Organized community and civic participation begins well before voting age
milestones.researchNote: Needed: a verbatim sentence naming the ages at which children and adolescents take part in organized school, community or neighborhood groups. Candidates to fetch: the National Household Education Survey parent and family involvement tables on nces.ed.gov; Census Current Population Survey Civic Engagement and Volunteering Supplement detailed tables on census.gov, whose published age bands start at the teenage years and may not reach younger children at all.
milestones.windowInWords: Group and community participation starts in childhood, long before the age at which the right to vote attaches, but the age band could not be sourced with a verbatim figure in this pass.
